depositBoxId.description: The box the cash moved in or out of. Set on every lift `withdrawFromDepositBox` records (26 September, pull audit R099).

witnessPrincipalId.description: The cashier who countersigned a withdrawal. Null on other movements.

authorisedByPrincipalId.description: The principal who authorised the movement, recorded for audit.

sequence.description: Monotonic within the shift. Preserves order across an offline batch.

ChangeCredentialRequest.description: Request only. The credential itself is stored hashed in `identity.principal_credential` (`PrincipalCredential`, CHG-CRD-001) and is never returned by any operation (`handoff/schema-storage-only.md`).

method.description: Which credential is being changed (`PrincipalCredential.method`). Card, RFID and SSO are not secrets the principal holds, so they are not changed here.

currentCredential.description: Compared with the current `credentialHash` and never stored. A wrong one is 422 `current-credential-wrong`, and counts towards the lockout like a wrong sign-in.

newCredential.description: Stored as the new `credentialHash` (a PHC string, ADR-0071); the replaced hash moves to `identity.principal_credential_history`. A PIN is digits only, exactly `PasswordPolicy.pinLength` long.

countedCash.description: **The cashier's blind count, one line per denomination counted** (decided 29 September, readiness close-out; our build plan). The server writes each line as one `CashCountLine` (`countKind` close) against the shift, taking the face value from `platform.denomination`. A denomination may appear once; a repeat is refused with 422 `duplicate-denomination`.

nonCashDeclared.description: Declared totals per non-cash tender, for reconciliation against captured payments.

notes.description: The cashier's note on the count. Asked of every cashier on a blind count, never only after a variance is shown (CHG-FIN-003, DI-803).

cashierReason.description: Anything the cashier knows went wrong in the shift (DI-803: till error, unrecorded refund, miscount, other). Optional and given without seeing the variance (CHG-FIN-003); the supervisor reads it beside the variance on BO-040. **Optional here, never skipped where it matters** (CHG-R4-019): if the count differs within the threshold and this is empty, the shift waits for `giveShiftVarianceReason` before it closes.

releaseHeldLeases.description: Return unsold inventory leases held by this workstation (ADR-0013 C103). Closing without releasing strands capacity until TTL expiry, which is visible at a gate during peak.

CountedDenominationLine.x-ticvai-persistence: none — request only; lands as `CashCountLine` rows
CountedDenominationLine.description:
**One line of a cash count as the cashier types it: which note or coin, how many, and what they come to** (decided 29 September, readiness close-out; our build plan). The shape of the blind count on close (`closeShift`) and of the count columns on the till screens (POS-007, POS-011). It is the request side of `CashCountLine`, which is the stored row and adds the shift, the count kind, who counted and when.
**`total` is shown to the cashier and checked, not trusted**: the server recomputes `count` times the denomination's face value and refuses a line whose `total` disagrees with 422 `count-total-mismatch`. An inactive or unknown denomination is refused with 422 `unknown-denomination`.

denominationId.description: References `platform.denomination` (`Denomination.id`) — face value, kind and counting order live there.

count.description: **How many of this note or coin were counted.** Zero is a line, not an omission: a denomination counted and found empty.

total.description: `count` times the face value, in the denomination's currency. Optional on the way in (the server computes it) and checked when sent. Stored as `orders.cash_count_line.counted_value` (r8 integration, CHG-R8INT-005).

denominations.description: **Stored as `orders.cash_count_line` rows** with `countKind: movement` and this movement's `cashMovementId`, not as a column. The jsonb blob this used to land in is what `Denomination` was created to replace (26 September, pull audit R099).

reference.description: Safe drop reference or bag number.

priority.description: **Optional since 29 September** (M17-01). Sent, it is `manual` and wins. Absent, the asset's `priorityOverride` applies, and failing that the venue's `WorkOrderPriorityPolicy` scores the fault.

requiredQualificationCodes.description: Skills the job needs, as qualification codes; `suggestWorkOrderAssignee` ranks by them (M17-13).

attachmentRefs.description: Photo-first. Expected at creation, not added later from memory.

takeAssetOutOfService.description: Raise and immediately suspend the asset. For a fault found on a live ride, the two are one action.

DenyReason.description:
Enumerated so the client can render an appropriate operator prompt. A gate operator facing a queue needs a reason and a next action, not a boolean.

**`capacityReached` is "Venue full"** (12 October 2026, CHG-R6-036): an entry-direction scan is denied when the current count of the access point's area, or of any area above it up to the venue (entries minus exits plus `operationalAdjustment`), is at or above that area's `capacity`, set with `setAccessAreaCapacity`. An area whose capacity is null never denies for capacity; an exit is never denied for it.

incidentNumber.description: **Server-assigned: the venue prefix plus a sequence per venue** (decided 28 September, audit R152). Not gapless; only tax invoices are gapless, per legal entity.

isReportable.description: Requires notification to an external authority within a statutory window.

notifiedAt.description: The earliest `notifiedAt` among this incident's authority notifications. **Maintained on write** by `recordAuthorityNotification`; each notification itself is a row of `maintenance.incident_authority_notification`.

escalation.description: **Set while the incident is escalated** (the optional Escalated step of the 3 October flow; CHG-RUL-011). Screens show "Escalated" when `status` is `underInvestigation` and this is set. Cleared when the incident closes.

reopenCount.description: How many times the incident was reopened (CHG-RUL-011). Each reopen is a logged row.

IncidentAuthorityNotification.description: **One notification to an external authority, appended by `recordAuthorityNotification`.** An incident may be reported to more than one authority, or to the same one twice, and each is the evidence that an obligation was met — so each is a row, not an overwrite of `maintenance.incident.notified_at`.

description.description: The original report. Never edited — investigation adds to the record.

investigationNote.description: The latest entry of `investigationNotes`, kept for readers that show one line.

investigationNotes.description: **Every investigation note, oldest first** (decided 28 September, audit R106 (5)). Read from `maintenance.incident_investigation_note`; appended by `updateIncident`.

involvedParties.description: Who was involved, as given in `ReportIncidentRequest.involvedSubjectIds` and `involvedStaffPrincipalIds`. Read from `maintenance.incident_involved_party`.

IncidentInvestigationNote.description: **One investigation note, appended by `updateIncident`** (decided 28 September, audit R106 (5)). A history rather than a field, so what an investigator thought on Tuesday survives what they found on Thursday.

kind.description: **Every change is logged here** (CHG-RUL-011): an investigator's note, or a row the server writes for a status change, an escalation or a reopen, with `note` as its reason.

IncidentInvolvedParty.description: **One person involved in an incident, by opaque reference.** A guest or member of the public is a `pii.subject` id — personal details live there, the erasable store of ADR-0023, so the incident record survives an erasure request intact. A member of staff is a principal id. Exactly one of the two is set, as `kind` says.

role.description: The person's part in the incident, from `addIncidentPerson` (CHG-RUL-013).

contactStored.description: Whether a contact is held for the person: only with their consent to be contacted (`AddIncidentPersonRequest.contactConsent`; CHG-RUL-013).

IncidentMedia.description: **One photo, video or document on an incident** (`uploadIncidentMedia`; CHG-RUL-013). The file is in the media store; this row links it to the incident.

status.description: `stored` once the media store confirmed the transfer and `assetRef` is set.

upload.description: The signed upload, as `assets.createUpload` returns it; only on the 201.

InventoryStockReservation.description: **Taken from the backend workbook, 20 September.** Temporarily reserves stock for an order or operational requirement so it cannot be allocated elsewhere.

sourceId.description: The id of what the stock is reserved for: a work order, a rental agreement or an order. A uuid, as every id is (ADR-0056); it was text from 29 September to 30 September because a work order id was then 26-character text (M17-02).

LoginRequest.description: **`workstationId` is required for a device door and absent from a browser door** (CHG-DOOR-001, 2 October 2026). It was required on every login, so no browser could sign in: the TICVAI Console (ADM-001), Venue Management (SUP-001) and the partner portal (PTR-001) have no workstation. Optional in the schema is additive against r1; the rule moved to where it belongs, the device-bound methods: `pin`, `card` and `rfid` without a `workstationId` are refused 400 (`workstation-required`). A `password` sign-in from a till, handheld or scanner still sends it, because the workstation decides the Sale Board, the hardware and the till identity (never a permission, ADR-0002).

credential.description: The password for `password`; the PIN for `pin`, `card` and `rfid`. Compared with the principal's `PrincipalCredential.credentialHash` (method `password` or `pin`) and never stored (ADR-0071, CHG-CRD-003). A badge carries no secret: see `method`.

method.description:
**`pin` is how a till is actually used.** A cashier signs in at a shared terminal between guests, and a password on a touchscreen with somebody waiting is a password that gets shortened, shared or written on the drawer. The employee number goes in `username` and the PIN in `credential`, so the shape of the request does not change — only what the operator types.

**A PIN is weaker than a password and the difference is bounded by the device, not by the secret.** A `pin` (like `card` and `rfid`) is accepted only with a `workstationId`, refused 400 `workstation-required` without one (CHG-DOOR-001), and the workstation is *NOT a permission source*: it says which till, and the till is on a venue network in a staff area. A PIN is a reasonable credential there and nowhere else, which is why this is an enum value and not a policy flag — a surface that wants it has to ask for it by name.

Added 10 September 2026 for `POS-000 Sign In`.

**`card` and `rfid` say how the username was entered, not a credential of their own** (R8 blocker IDENTITY-C36, CHG-R8MIG-006; the lead's answer, option C). A badge tap at POS-000 or SCN-001 fills `username` with the employee number the badge carries, and the operator still types the PIN in `credential`, which is checked against the principal's `pin` credential exactly as for `pin`. No badge token is stored and `PrincipalCredential.method` stays `password` or `pin`. **`sso` is not a login method**: an SSO sign-in goes through `startSsoAuthorization` and `completeSsoAuthorization`, and a `login` with `method` `sso` is refused 400.

workstationId.description:
Identifies the device. Determines Sale Board, connected hardware, till identity and Access Point inheritance. NOT a permission source.

**Sent by a device door, never by a browser** (CHG-DOOR-001, 2 October 2026). Required in effect for the device-bound methods `pin`, `card` and `rfid` (400 `workstation-required` without it); absent on the TICVAI Console, Venue Management and partner portal sign-ins, which have no workstation.

mustChangeCredential.description: **The credential just used is temporary** (14 October 2026, CHG-CRD-001, ADAM CR-078): the principal's `Principal.mustChangeCredential`, set at creation and by `resetPrincipalCredential`. While it is true the session may call `changeOwnCredential` and `logout` and nothing else; **a successful `changeOwnCredential` leaves the same session pending on the second factor when `requiresMfa`, and then `enrolMfaMethod`, `verifyMfaEnrolment`, `createMfaChallenge` and `verifyMfaChallenge` are allowed, then role selection** (R8 blocker fix, IDENTITY-C03, lead answer A: new credential first, then the second factor, then the role); the door asks for the new password or PIN (ADM-001, SUP-001, PTR-001, EMP-001, SCN-001, POS-000) before the role prompt and the landing. A successful `changeOwnCredential` clears it. Always false for a single sign-on principal.

requiresMfa.description: True when the principal holds any permission listed in `PasswordPolicy.mfaRequiredForPermissions` (decided 28 September, audit R135). The session is not usable until `verifyMfaChallenge` succeeds on a `signIn` challenge.

hasMfaMethod.description: Whether the principal has an active MFA method. With `requiresMfa` true and this false, the client must enrol one first (audit R135, R126 (5)).

mfaMethods.description: The principal's active methods, so the client can offer the right one for the `signIn` challenge. Empty when `requiresMfa` is false.

MfaMethod.description: **A second factor a principal or a guest has enrolled** (R8 blockers IDENTITY-C12 and IDENTITY-C34, CHG-R8MIG-007). Exactly one of `principalId` and `subjectId` is set, so a guest's method is stored like a staff member's and `GuestSession.requiresMfa` and `mfaMethods` are answered from here; the row is its owner's alone (`x-ticvai-rls: own-row`). Three fields are storage only and never returned (`handoff/schema-storage-only.md`): `secret` (a `totp` shared secret, which `verifyMfaChallenge` computes the code from), `destination` (the full phone number or email an `smsOtp` or `emailOtp` code is sent to; `maskedTarget` is the only form returned) and `pendingExpiresAt` (set while an enrolment awaits `verifyMfaEnrolment`; an expired pending row is deleted by the next `enrolMfaMethod` of its owner).

principalId.x-ticvai-staff-only: Omitted from the response when the caller is a guest (R164; r8 gate residue, CHG-R8RES-008). A guest's own method has it null, so a guest screen never shows it.
principalId.description: The principal who enrolled it; null for a guest.

subjectId.description: The guest who enrolled it; null for a principal.

secret.description: The `totp` shared secret, encrypted with the tenant's field key (ADR-0063); null for other kinds. Never returned after `MfaEnrolment.secret`. This is the encrypted column ADAM CR-173 asked for (option A, accepted 21 October 2026; in the package since r8, CHG-R8INT-024; CHG-R10ID-008), which `verifyMfaEnrolment` and `verifyMfaChallenge` decrypt to compute the expected code.

destination.description: The full phone number (`smsOtp`) or email (`emailOtp`) the code goes to, encrypted with the tenant's field key (ADR-0063); null for other kinds. Only `maskedTarget` is ever returned.

pendingExpiresAt.description: While `isActive` is false, when the unconfirmed enrolment lapses; null once verified.

maskedTarget.description: Partially masked destination, so a person can tell two methods apart.

involvedSubjectIds.description: Opaque references. Personal details live in the erasable store, so the incident record survives an erasure request intact.

isPrimary.description: True for the role that is the principal's `primaryRoleId` (`identity.principal.primary_role_id`); false for the others (14 October 2026, ADAM CR-077; CHG-IDR-002).

grantId.description: **The grant this card stands for** (`identity.delegated_access.id`; IDENTITY-C45, CHG-R8SPN-032). A role held at two venues is two grants and two cards; `selectRole` takes the chosen one.

scope.description: The scope node the grant is held at (`platform.scope`), with its name, so the card can say which venue (IDENTITY-C45).

ServiceSummary.x-ticvai-persistence: none — computed from fnb.table_visit, the orders and payments on it

openTables.description: Visits still open, with their bills not yet settled.

scope.description: Scope nodes this session may act within, resolved once at login from the ltree hierarchy with deny-overrides-allow. Clients filter navigation against this — they never compute it.

effectivePermissions.description: Flattened set across all granted scopes, after deny resolution. Convenience for coarse checks only: it never decides an operation by itself (ADAM CR-189). Anything scope-sensitive uses `permissionsByScope`.

permissionsByScope.description:
Permissions effective at each granted scope path, after deny resolution. Clients filter navigation on this and never compute permissions themselves.

**The server keeps the same set and authorises from it** (decided 25 October 2026, Chinmay, ADAM CR-189 option A; CHG-R10ID-001). The rule for every operation: `x-ticvai-permission` is evaluated at the scope the operation acts on, from the per-scope set (the node acted on or one of its ancestors); `effectivePermissions` is for coarse checks only. A list's reach is the scope paths where its permission holds, and a filter outside it is `403`; a tenant-level operation needs its permission at the tenant root. The request kernel's seam carries this set beside the flat one (#27692 owns the field) and sign-in (#27666) fills it from the same resolution that fills this property; tests fill the seam until sign-in lands. The full statement is `docs/architecture/specs/permission-resolution.md` section 7.2. No wire shape changes.

saleBoardId.description:
Landing surface, derived from the WORKSTATION, not the role (12 Aug 2026 §3). Ticketing, F&B or Retail board.

**Optional since 2 October 2026: only a till session carries it** (Chinmay, door follow-ups; CHG-CSP-002; breaking change against r1 approved as BC-001 to BC-005 in `docs/active/breaking-changes.yaml`). A browser door (ADM-001, SUP-001, PTR-001) and a staff handheld (EMP-001) sign in with no workstation since CHG-DOOR-001, so they have no board to land on and the field is absent. On a till it is the workstation's effective board: the outlet's board unless the till overrides it (`tenancy.Workstation.saleBoardSource`; CHG-CSP-006). A client reads its landing from this field when present and from its own platform otherwise.

availableRoles.description: **The roles the principal may choose, one per grant** (IDENTITY-C45, CHG-R8SPN-032), resolved on read as `LoginResponse.availableRoles` is, so EMP-002 can list them on a cold open or after a relaunch (`getCurrentSession`) without signing in again.

expiresAt.description: When the session ends at the latest: `openedAt` plus `PasswordPolicy.sessionMaxHours` (12 hours by default; proposed, client to correct). A till session ends earlier, when the shift on its workstation closes; any session ends at `logout` or a revocation. Refreshing the access token never moves this time (IDENTITY-C25, FOUNDATION-AI-C27; CHG-R8SPN-014).

Shift.description: **`approvals` and `incidents` are child rows** (26 September, pull audit R099): `orders.pos_shift_approval` and `orders.pos_shift_incident`, one row per item, keyed to the shift. Until then the contract carried both and `orders.pos_shift` had nowhere to put either.

id.description: Client-generated UUIDv7. Also the idempotency key.

principalId.description: Who opened it. Cash reconciles to a person and a drawer.

incidents.description:
BL-097. **A till has exceptions and there was nowhere to write them** — a no-sale, a drawer opened without a transaction, a manager override, a guest dispute.
**This is the log a cash-up investigation starts from**, and a shift that balances with four unexplained no-sales is not a shift that balanced.

currency.description:
**Resolved from the region, not stored** (ADR-0018, 24 August). Region-scoped and not overri dable below, so a row in a UAE region is AED and cannot be anything else. **Kept on the wire , removed from the table** — a client should not walk a hierarchy to read a figure, and the  database should not hold nine million copies of AED. Four tables genuinely differ from their
 region and keep a stored currency: `orders.payment.tender_currency`, `inventory.supplier`, 
`ledger.account`, `control.partner_agreement`.

currencyScale.description:
**Resolved from the region, not stored** (ADR-0018, 24 August). Region-scoped and not overri dable below, so a row in a UAE region is AED and cannot be anything else — storing it per ro w is a copy of a fact that cannot differ. **Kept on the wire, removed from the table**: a cl ient reading a figure should not walk a hierarchy to know what it means, and the database sh ould not hold nine million copies of AED. Four tables genuinely differ from their region and
 keep a stored currency — `orders.payment.tender_currency`, `inventory.supplier`, `ledger.ac
count`, `control.partner_agreement`. **A guest paying USD at an AED venue is a real row; a w orkstation with its own currency is a misconfiguration.**

salesTotal.description: What the till took in sales, as the guest paid it — tax included: the shift's takings, not Gross sales (CHG-FIN-002, CHG-FIN-010). **Shown to the shift's own cashier only as one total across every tender** ("Sales this shift" on POS-025; the lead, 3 October 2026, CHG-RONEC-002): with no cash share it cannot be turned into the expected cash, so the blind close holds (CHG-FIN-003). The cash share, the tender split, `expectedCash` and `variance` stay with the supervisor.

refundsTotal.description: What the till paid back, as the guest was refunded it — tax included.

liftsTotal.description: Cash taken out mid-shift by lifts and withdrawals. Cash, so neither gross nor net.

expectedCash.description: 26 September, pull audit R207. **The figure the blind count was measured against**, revealed once the count is in — null until then. Until this date only `ShiftCloseResult` carried it, returned once by `closeShift`, so BO-040 could not show the over/short it exists to accept. **Null to the shift's own cashier on every read** (CHG-FIN-003, 2 October): returned only to a caller holding OVERSHORT_ACCEPT or SHIFT_CLOSE_OTHER at the venue.

countedCash.description: What the close count found. Null until the shift is counted.

variance.description: Counted minus expected, as `ShiftCloseResult.variance`. Negative is short. Null to the shift's own cashier, as `expectedCash` (CHG-FIN-003).

cashierReason.description: What the cashier said went wrong, given with the blind count (`CloseShiftRequest.cashierReason`, DI-803) without seeing the variance; the supervisor reads it beside the variance on BO-040 (CHG-FIN-003).

cashierNote.description: The cashier's note with the count (`CloseShiftRequest.notes`; CHG-FIN-003).

varianceReasonRequired.description: **Computed, not stored** (CHG-R4-019): true while the shift is `pendingClosure` because its count differs from the expected figure within the threshold and no `cashierReason` is recorded. The till shows "Give a reason to close" (POS-007, EMP-009), BO-040 and BO-043 list it as waiting for a reason; `giveShiftVarianceReason` or `approveShiftClose` clears it. Shown to the shift's own cashier, since it carries no figure (CHG-FIN-003).

heldLeaseCount.description: Inventory leases currently held by this workstation. Surfaced so an operator closing a shift can see what will be returned.

businessDate.description: **The business day the shift belongs to** (12 October 2026, CHG-R6-032): the venue-local date of `openedAt` taken against the venue's `businessDayCutoff` (tenancy `VenueSettings`, inheriting the tenant default, default 00:00). Set once when the shift opens and never moved, so a shift opened at 23:00 and closed at 01:00 stays on the day it opened. The daily reconciliation (BO-043) lists the shifts of one business date, and the period close's `noOpenShifts` check reads it (finance).

recordedAt.description: When the device recorded the open. `openedAt` is the server's time.

suspendReason.description: The `reason` given to `suspendShift`. Cleared on resume.

closedByPrincipalId.description: Who submitted the close count. `reopenShift` refuses an approver who is this principal, and until 26 September there was nothing to compare against (pull audit R099).

recountRequestedAt.description: **Set by `rejectShiftVariance`, cleared by the cashier's recount** (decided 2 October 2026, Chinmay; DEC-175; CHG-CSP-013; DI-804). While set, the shift is `pendingVariance` waiting for the cashier rather than the supervisor: the cashier's view says "Recount requested" instead of "Under review".

recountRequestedByPrincipalId.description: The supervisor who sent the count back (CHG-CSP-013).

recountReason.description: The supervisor's reason, shown to the cashier; never an amount (CHG-CSP-013, CHG-FIN-003).

countNumber.description: How many close counts the shift has had: 0 before the first, 1 after it, 2 after a recount (CHG-CSP-013). The latest is the one measured.

syncedAt.description: Null while the shift has unsynced operations.

kind.description: `open` from `approveShiftOpen`, `close` from `approveShiftClose`, `variance` from `acceptShiftVariance`, `reopen` from `reopenShift` (the supervisor who signed it, the time and the `reason`).

ShiftCountReceipt.description: **What `submitShiftCount` returns to the cashier: what happens next, never the figure** (CHG-FIN-003). No expected cash, no variance, no over or short.

outcome.description: `closed`: within the venue's threshold, the shift is closed. `referredToSupervisor`: a supervisor reviews the count (`pendingVariance`); the till says "Your count is with your supervisor" and nothing about the amount. `awaitingCloseApproval`: the venue supervises every close (`pendingClosure`), or, with `varianceReasonRequired` true, the shift waits for the cashier's reason for a difference within the threshold (CHG-R4-019).

countNumber.description: 1 for the first count of the close, 2 for a recount the supervisor asked for, and so on.

varianceReasonRequired.description: **The count found a difference within the threshold and no reason came with it** (the client's policy of 6 October 2026, T10.1; CHG-R4-019). The shift is held in `pendingClosure` (outcome `awaitingCloseApproval`) and the till asks for a reason (`giveShiftVarianceReason`), which closes it. Says only that a difference exists: never its amount or direction, and the count is already locked (CHG-FIN-003). False when the count matched, when a `cashierReason` came with it, and beyond the threshold (`referredToSupervisor`).

ShiftVarianceReasonRequest.description: The reason for a difference within the threshold, given after the blind count is locked (`giveShiftVarianceReason`; the client's policy of 6 October 2026, T10.1; CHG-R4-019).

reason.description: The same reasons as `CloseShiftRequest.cashierReason` (DI-803), recorded as the shift's `cashierReason`.

note.description: What happened, in the cashier's words; recorded as the shift's `cashierNote` (appended to a note given with the count). Required when `reason` is `other` (422 `reason-note-required`).

isEnforced.description: True disables password login for principals covered by this provider.

scopePath.description:
**The partition key** (ADR-0005). Added 31 August: the operations that write this table declare a scope and the table carried no column for it — **49 tables were in that state**, so a row could be written at venue scope and then read by anything that could reach the table.

**`scope_path` rather than a specific id** because it is prefix-comparable: `uae.dubai` contains `uae.dubai.marina`, and one index answers every level of the walk.

**Operations write it at `tenant` scope**; the server sets it and ignores it in a request.

StockReservationSourceType.description: What a stock reservation is for (decided 17 September, M17-02; `rentalAgreement` is the existing use from `rental.agreement_item`; `retailReservation` is Retail's `reserveMerchandise`, whose reservation id is `sourceId`, R8 blocker APPROVALS-TENANCY-C34).

SupervisorStepUp.description:
**A supervisor signs the act in place, on the device making the call** (decided 28 September, audit R144). Used where the decision is a same-device step-up rather than an approval request: reopening a shift, recounting a stock count, a retail return above the venue threshold, and (proposed by the coordinator, client to confirm) closing a stock transfer short and cancelling a performance.

**The verification rule, the same on every operation that takes it:** the server checks `credential` against `principalId`; that principal must hold the operation's `x-ticvai-permission` at the operation's scope, must be active at that venue, and must not be the person whose act is being reversed where the operation says so. Any failure is a `403` (`supervisor-step-up-refused`) and nothing is written. **No approval request is raised**, and the operation declares `x-ticvai-step-up: pin`.

**Where `principalId` comes from, on every operation that takes this** (decided 20 October 2026, Chinmay, R8 blocker cause GPS-C31, option A; CHG-R8SPN-035). The PIN prompt shows a picker filled by `identity.listStepUpSupervisors` with the operation's permission: the active principals who hold it at the caller's venue, by display name. The supervisor picks their own name and types their PIN; the prompt sends the picked `principalId` (or, where the prompt asks for an employee number instead, `supervisorUsername`). **Nobody signs their own act**: a `principalId` (or resolved `supervisorUsername`) equal to the caller's own principal is refused `403 supervisor-step-up-refused`, even when the caller holds the permission, and the picker leaves the caller out.

principalId.description: The supervisor signing. Recorded against the act. **Exactly one of `principalId` or `supervisorUsername`** is sent (neither, or both, is `400`; not in the schema as a oneOf, so an r1 client still validates).

supervisorUsername.description: **The supervisor's employee number**, which is what the step-up prompt asks for (R8 blocker fix, IDENTITY-C44). The server resolves it to the principal (`identity.principal.username`, within the tenant) before it checks the PIN; an unknown one is refused exactly as a wrong PIN, `403 supervisor-step-up-refused`, so the prompt does not reveal which employee numbers exist. The act is recorded against the resolved principal. Exactly one of this or `principalId`.

credential.description: The supervisor's staff PIN, as they sign in at a till with it. **A PIN, never a password** (audit R123 (7)). Never stored or returned. Exactly the tenant's `PasswordPolicy.pinLength` digits (4, 6 or 8, the tenant's choice; CHG-CRD-002), which the prompt's keypad takes from `WorkstationContext.pinLength`. The operation never reads Identity's tables to check it; it asks Identity's `verifySupervisorStepUp` query (`x-ticvai-read-via`, CHG-CRD-004), and a wrong PIN counts towards `PasswordPolicy.pinLockoutAfterAttempts` as at sign-in.

TicketStatus.x-ticvai-persistence: none — computed from entitlement and scans
TicketStatus.description:
**A validation result, not a lifecycle**, despite the name. Computed at scan time from the entitlement and its scan history — `isValid`, `entriesUsed`, `isInsideVenue`.
**The name misled a state model into anchoring on it** (`states/entitlement.yaml`, removed 18 August): six lifecycle states were checked against an object with no values, and `check-states` warned about it for a day before anyone read the schema.
The entitlement's lifecycle is `orders.EntitlementStatus`. **This is what a gate learns when it scans**, which is a different question with a similar name.

ticketId.description: Stable for the life of the ticket, independent of the media carrying it.

holderName.description: Present only where the entitlement is name-bound. Identity and entitlement are separate concerns; most entitlements carry no holder.

isInsideVenue.description: Derived from the last scan. Drives anti-passback evaluation.

issuingCellId.description: Present when this entitlement was issued in a different cell and is being redeemed here as a delegated right (ADR-0010). Null for locally issued tickets.

guestLinkId.description: Pseudonymous cross-region guest reference. Present only on delegated rights. Carries no personal data.

accessToken.description: JWT carrying `sid`, validated per request against the session registry.

expiresIn.description: Seconds until the access token expires: `PasswordPolicy.accessTokenMinutes` x 60, 900 by default (15 minutes; proposed, client to correct). The refresh token, its rotation and reuse detection, and the signing key are described once on `bearerAuth` in contracts/shared/common.yaml (IDENTITY-C25, FOUNDATION-AI-C27; CHG-R8SPN-014).

capturedAt.description: Device time the photo or video was taken.

id.description: Client-generated UUIDv7. Also the idempotency key and dedupe key.

mediaCode.description: What was read from the media. NOT the ticket id — media can be re-linked over a ticket's life.

groupSize.description: For group media admitting several holders on one read.

proximityToken.description: BLE proximity assertion where the venue requires the operator to be physically at the gate. Absent where not configured.

recordedAt.description: Device time of the read. Authoritative for ordering, not for validity.

denyDetail.description: Human-readable, localised. For operator display, never for logic.

denyCause.description: **The finer cause of three denials decided on 2 October 2026**, beside the r1 `denyReason` a client already switches on (a new `DenyReason` value would be a breaking change against r1; CHG-CSP-026, CHG-CSP-030, CHG-CSP-035). `attractionTemporarilyClosed` (DEC-228): `denyReason` `outsideAdmissionWindow`, with `reopensAt` and `queueReturnOffer`. `timeBoundWindowElapsed` (DEC-232): a time-bound entitlement scanned after its window from first scan, `denyReason` `expired`. `offlineLimitExceeded` (DEC-426): a reader offline longer than the venue's `AccessOfflinePolicy.maxOfflineDurationHours` refusing a tap it cannot check, `denyReason` `outsideAdmissionWindow`. Null for every other denial.

reopensAt.description: When a temporarily closed attraction expects to reopen, where known (DEC-228; CHG-CSP-026).

queueReturnOffer.description: A virtual-queue return window offered at a denied scan of a temporarily closed attraction, where the venue enables it (DEC-228; CHG-CSP-026). Taking it is `queue.joinQueue`.

admittedCount.description: Holders admitted on this read. Differs from groupSize on partial admission.

advisory.description:
BL-179, CF-130. **What a device observed, for the steward, never for the gate.** Present only where an access point's device reports the matching `DeviceCapability` and the venue has turned the corresponding setting on.
**Never persisted.** This schema is computed and stored as `access.scan_event`, and the advisory is deliberately not part of what is stored: an inferred classification kept against a guest is sensitive personal data with no consent behind it. **A guest agreed to be admitted, not to be classified** — Face Pass and Face Tag carry `consent_purpose_id` and `consent_given_at` because somebody enrolled, and nobody enrols in being looked at by a turnstile. `scan_event` records that an override happened and never what the device thought, which keeps `overrideRateAlertThreshold` working without building a register nobody agreed to.
**It cannot reach `outcome` or `denyReason`.** Those are decisive and `entitlementGated` is `true` and read-only: the gate admits on the entitlement, and everything here sits on top of that without replacing any of it.

genderClassification.description: **`undetermined` is a real answer and the most common one to design for.** A classifier that never returns it is one that has been tuned to look confident.

confidence.description: **Required reading for the steward, not decoration.** An advisory with no confidence is read as a fact, and `overrideRateAlertThreshold` exists to catch exactly the failure that produces — *an override rate near zero means the steward has stopped deciding.* That number only means anything if the steward could see how sure the device was.

reportedByDeviceId.description: **Which device said it.** A classifier that degrades is one camera, not a venue, and an advisory nobody can trace to hardware cannot be investigated or switched off alone.

WithdrawalReason.description: Why a supervisor took cash out of a box. Set only on lifts `withdrawFromDepositBox` records.

downtimeMinutes.description:
**Measured from out-of-service to back-in-service, not from work start to work end.** A ride down for six hours of which two were spent working is down six hours, and the gap between the two numbers is the thing worth managing.
**Maintained on write**: set when the asset returns to service, as the minutes from the `maintenance.asset_status_change` row that took it out carrying this work order's id to the asset's next change back to `inService`. Null while the asset is still out, and for a work order that never took it out.

rootCause.description: **Structured, because free text cannot be counted.** *Deferred maintenance* is the value a venue least wants to see and most needs to — a fault caused by work that was postponed is an argument for a budget.

escalationLevel.description: **Escalation is a clock, not a decision.** A work order on a ride nobody has accepted after twenty minutes escalates itself, because the alternative is somebody noticing.

workOrderNumber.description: **Server-assigned: the venue prefix plus a sequence per venue** (decided 28 September, audit R152). Not gapless; only tax invoices are gapless, per legal entity.

assetName.description: The asset's name, copied when the work order is raised or its asset changes, and not updated when the asset is later renamed — the record reads as it was raised.

priorityScore.description: The score the venue's policy gave the fault when raised; null when a person or the asset set the priority (M17-01).

prioritySource.description: Where `priority` came from (M17-01). A change through `updateWorkOrder` makes it `manual`.

categoryId.description: As raised in `CreateWorkOrderRequest.categoryId`, amendable by `updateWorkOrder`. The category is what `completeWorkOrder` reads to decide whether completion photographs are required.

locationDescription.description: Where the fault is, as raised. Needed where there is no asset — a broken tile, a leak in a corridor.

elapsedMinutes.description: Labour minutes accumulated up to the last pause or stop. **Maintained on write** by `recordWorkOrderTime`, `pauseWorkOrder` and `completeWorkOrder`; while `isTimerRunning` is true the interval since the last start is not yet included.

isOverdue.description: `dueAt` is in the past and the status is still `open`, `assigned`, `inProgress`, `paused` or `awaitingParts`. **Computed on read and not stored** — it depends on the clock. `listWorkOrders?overdueOnly` applies the same test to `due_at`.

capturedAt.description: Device time. **Distinct from when it synced** — a photo taken at 09:14 in a basement and uploaded at 11:40 is evidence of the first, not the second.

reservedQuantity.description: Still reserved for this work order and not yet issued (M17-02).

completedByPrincipalId.description: Who called `completeWorkOrder`. **What `verifyWorkOrder` compares against** — the verifier may not be the technician who completed the work, and the assignee is not necessarily that person.

supersededByWorkOrderId.description: Set by `cancelWorkOrder` where the reason is `superseded`.

duplicateOfWorkOrderId.description: Set by `closeWorkOrder` where the outcome is `duplicate`.

WorkOrderFaultAssessment.description: What the person raising a fault says about it, which the priority score reads (M17-01).

accessPointId.description: Inherited from the workstation, never selected by the operator.

cellName.description: The cell this workstation's region is served from, which is the cell the commerce host answering this request is deployed in (one cell per tenant per region, ADR-0014): the host fills it from its own configuration and reads no table (ADAM CR-096, CHG-RTE-001). A client uses this only for diagnostics and telemetry tagging — never for routing, which the Control Plane resolves.

deploymentProfile.description: Whether this surface reads catalogue locally (ADR-0013). Determines which flows the client enables offline.

pinLength.description: **The tenant's `PasswordPolicy.pinLength`, carried to the device** (14 October 2026, CHG-CRD-002, ADAM CR-078). A device door draws its PIN keypad, and its supervisor step-up prompt, at this many digits; the device keeps it with the workstation context of the last session on it, so the door needs nothing fetched before sign-in. A device that has never had a session accepts 4 to 8 digits and the server decides. Read from `identity.password_policy`, not stored on the workstation.
